title: Influence of Robots’ Voice Naturalness on Trust and Compliance
edition: ACM Transactions on Human-Robot Interaction 14(2), Article 29 (2025), printed pp. 29:1–29:25

actor.method: Web-extracted author-hosted original PDF text and PDF rendered-page inspection
actor.independence: additional AI source check, NOT independent human/blinded screening

source_access.route: author-hosted public ACM article, CC BY 4.0 declared on first page
source_access.extent: selected passages from title/abstract, §§3.1–3.7, Appendices C–E; not a complete paper read, no sound playback

first_stage.scientific_status: additional noncanonical source recheck; integration owns TA admission and shared exports

phases.support: §3.2 describes six TTS voice samples rated for perceived voice quality and future robot suitability, rather than operational system-status/action messaging during the survey.
phases.limitation: Voice-sample lexical content/audio not independently inspected. E2=no is an AI-assisted interpretation of the described task, not an accepted exclusion.

phases.support: §3.4 describes a pilot assessing whether listeners distinguished the two voices and understood robot game rules/speech; methods and participant overlap with the main recruitment are insufficient to assert an independent comparative primary study.
phases.limitation: Pilot participants' identity, overlap, complete outcomes and design details are not independently verified.

phases.support: Robot issues live status/next-step guidance and selectable advice in a human-robot Battleship game; natural versus mechanical speech is the between-participant manipulation with identical gestures, utterances and facial-expression repertoire across arms; choices, response latencies and questionnaires are measured.
phases.limitation: Voice lines are embedded in multimodal interaction; conditional messages are repeated within each participant, not independent samples. This document does not assess effect sizes.

participant_identity.caution: The pre/main nonoverlap is author-reported, not a person-level verification; do not sum repeated trials, pilot, pre-study and main as independently verified samples.
